newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 8.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 8.5 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money was traded at around 8.5 percent on Monday morning, dealers said.
They said volumes were thin and operators seemed to be well prepared to face the approaching month-end.
One local bank dealer said early central bank injection of some 590 billion rupiah and carry-forward liquidity from last Friday kept the market flush.
One state bank dealer said some banks were bidding for central bank papers (SBIs) this morning, suggesting similar flush conditions on Tuesday.
She said there did not seem to be any worries of tightness despite weekly tax payments due Tuesday and the approaching month-end.
Dealers said one-week money was quoted at 12.75/13.00 percent and two-week money at 13.50/13.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 9.77 percent, compared with 8.43 percent on Thursday.
